raw_response:
Well, let me sit down and think this through. I've been working these 20 mu for over forty years now, so I know this land. The wheat-maize rotation is what we do here — has been since the eighties when the wells went in. My wife and I are still healthy enough to do most of the work, but our son is in Handan now with his family, sends money but isn't coming back to farm. So it's the two of us, and at 68 I have to be honest about what my back can take. That means I rely on the contracted machinery — combine harvester, planter, the works — for the heavy jobs.

**Wheat (winter wheat, all 20 mu)**

I'll plant Jimai 22 again around October 8-12, same as always. It does well on my soil, I've saved some seed but I buy fresh every two or three years from the agricultural supply store to keep vigor up. Sowing rate about 15 kg/mu — a bit on the heavy side because I'm planting late-ish and want good stand establishment.

For fertilizer, I learned at the township training session years ago to split nitrogen between base and topdress. I put down about 40 kg/mu of compound (15-15-15) before deep plowing — that gives roughly 6 kg N, 6 P, 6 K base. Then at jointing in late March, I topdress 15 kg urea per mu — that's about 7 more kg N. Total around 13 kg N/mu. Some of my neighbors put on 18-20, but my soil has been built up over years of straw return, and I haven't seen yield benefit from going higher. Last year I got 510 kg/mu, that's good for me.

Irrigation: I'll water at sowing if the autumn is dry (it usually is now), then jointing in March, then again at heading in late April, and one more at grain-filling if we don't get good rain in May. So 3-4 times. Each watering runs me 30-35 yuan/mu in electricity, so I don't waste them — I check the soil and the forecast.

For pests, the main worry is aphids and stripe rust. I'll do one combined spray at flag-leaf stage with insecticide and a triazole. If powdery mildew shows up early I'll spray a second time, but usually one is enough.

**Maize (summer maize, all 20 mu)**

The window is brutal — wheat off around June 10-12, maize has to go in within a week. I hire the combine and the no-till planter together, that's the only way at my age. Zhengdan 958 or Denghai 605, whatever the dealer has — both are reliable hybrids for this area. About 4 kg/mu seed, plant rate roughly 4500 plants/mu.

Fertilizer for maize: I do one shot at planting with the seeder placement — about 50 kg/mu of a 26-10-12 compound, that gives me 13 kg N as the base. Then if the maize looks pale at the big-flare stage (around V10), I'll side-dress 10 kg urea per mu, which adds another 4-5 kg N. Total maybe 17-18 kg N/mu. Maize is hungrier than wheat in my experience, and it pays back when you feed it.

Irrigation: depends on July-August rain. Usually I need one watering at tasseling/silking — that's the critical stage and you cannot skip it. If August is dry, one more at grain-fill. So 1-2 times.

Spray once at the whorl stage for armyworm and corn borer. Pre-emergent herbicide right after planting — atrazine plus acetochlor, that's standard.

Yield target around 520 kg/mu. Last year it was 540, year before 490 because of that hot spell in August.

**Overall thinking**

I'm being conservative because at my age I can't afford a bad year — there's no off-farm income coming in, just our pensions and what the land gives us. But I'm also not under-applying inputs the way some of the really old smallholders do, because I learned the technical side and I know the difference 5 kg of urea makes when the crop needs it. The straw return system over many years means my soil is in decent shape, so I can run a bit leaner on phosphorus and potassium than the recommendations.
